tools.name: ctx_note
tools.description: Session notes are pending intentions: work you intend to return to, with findings attached ("take a note" always qualifies). Not active steps, an executing plan, or restart insurance; a record of how things stand (world-state, a design at a time) with nothing to do about it goes stale silently; a fact worth keeping is memory, the rest is nothing. First line = title (<80 chars). write saves; read lists rows (note_ids for bodies); update changes one; dismiss retires 1–50. Dismiss a note when its work lands or is abandoned; a queue you never dismiss from stops being read. surface_condition parks it until an outside check against repo files, git, GitHub or the web holds.

content.description: Note text: first line title (<80 chars), then detail.

surface_condition.description: A condition an outside checker can verify on its own, periodically (repository, releases, web — anything it can look up); never something only this conversation knows.

filter.description: Read filter: all, active, pending, ready, dismissed. Omitted: active notes plus every current smart note (pending included); active: only active-status notes.

note_ids.description: One id for update, 1–50 for dismiss, or 1–50 to read those notes in full. Write and a plain read take an empty list.

tools.name: ctx_memory
tools.description: Durable facts about this project, shared with every agent on it and kept for months; active ones are in <project-memory> as `#id: fact`. Write one standalone fact when it must not have to be found again — a rule, an architecture fact, a constraint, a config value, a naming convention — especially what cost you turns. A pending intention with evidence is ctx_note, not memory. write (content + category); update one id (content; category optional); archive one or more ids (reason optional); merge two or more ids (content); get 1–20 ids in any status.

content.description: One standalone fact (write, update, merge). Archive and get: empty string.

category.description: Kind of fact (write; on update/merge pass the current category to keep it). Archive and get ignore it.

ids.description: Ids from <project-memory>: one for update, 1+ for archive, 2+ for merge, 1–20 for get. Write: empty list.

tools.name: ctx_search
tools.description:
Search the archive. Classic retrieval filters memories already in <project-memory> and the live tail. Phrase a question with expected terms; Chinese: 2-4 char terms, not a full sentence. Sources (omit for all): memory (rules), message (compacted; ordinals for ctx_expand), git_commit (commits), primer (project Q&A), note (follow-ups). Memory ids alone resolve directly; from/to restrict all sources to inclusive UTC dates.
With the memory cache on (OpenCode/Pi), source-less or memory+other queries may answer from synthesized memory plus non-memory summaries (memory may already be visible); mixed sources use classic minus memory; sources:["memory"] hits the bank directly (a miss is terminal); [], from/to and id queries go classic; limit still routes to the cache, bounding classic material and fallback only. The Rust module always uses classic.

query.description: A natural-language question carrying the exact terms you expect in the answer.

sources.description: Restrict to these sources; omit or [] for all.

system_text.text:
## Magic Context

`ctx_search` searches this project's archive — what earlier sessions said and decided, commits and notes; ask it before asking the user anything that may already be recorded, phrased as a question with the exact names in it. `ctx_memory` pins facts that stay true for the months this work lasts, for you and every agent on the project: what must not have to be found again, especially what cost you turns. They are not shown to you automatically; recall them with `ctx_search`. `ctx_note` is the tray for work you intend to return to, with its findings attached; findings without an intention are not a note; "take a note" from the user always goes there.
